Answer: A lightning-induced surge can arc through the thin wall
CSST has a thin corrugated wall; an indirect lightning strike can energize the system and arc through it. Direct bonding to the grounding electrode system is required.

title: GAS: Appliances installed in a garage where vehicles are parked must have ignition sources located at least:
text:
Appliances installed in a garage where vehicles are parked must have ignition sources located at least:
Answer: 18 inches above the floor
Ignition sources in garages must be at least 18 inches above the floor, since gasoline vapors are heavier than air and collect low. Physical protection from vehicle impact is also required.

title: GAS: Which section of 248 CMR governs large gas utilization equipment?
text:
Which section of 248 CMR governs large gas utilization equipment?
Answer: 248 CMR 7.00
248 CMR 7.00 covers large gas utilization equipment.

title: GAS: A gas appliance connector (flex) may:
text:
A gas appliance connector (flex) may:
Answer: Be used only for the length permitted, without passing through walls, floors, or partitions
Listed flexible connectors may not pass through walls, floors, ceilings, or partitions, may not be concealed, and may not be spliced together to gain length.

title: GAS: Before placing an appliance in service after gas work, the technician must:
text:
Before placing an appliance in service after gas work, the technician must:
Answer: Leak-check, verify manifold pressure, and confirm proper venting/combustion
Commissioning includes a leak check, verifying operating/manifold pressure against the rating plate, and confirming proper draft, venting, and combustion air before the appliance is left in service.

title: GENERAL: Under 248 CMR 11.02, how many clock hours of qualifying work experience must an apprentice accrue for each year in which they obtain 165 clock hours of education?
text:
Under 248 CMR 11.02, how many clock hours of qualifying work experience must an apprentice accrue for each year in which they obtain 165 clock hours of education?
Answer: 1,700 clock hours
Per 248 CMR 11.02, for each year in which an apprentice obtains 165 clock hours of education (one and a half tiers), that apprentice must accrue 1,700 clock hours of qualifying work experience as a licensed apprentice. Four such years produce the 6,800 hours required for the journeyman exam.

title: GENERAL: How many total clock hours of tier education are required for journeyman licensure in Massachusetts?
text:
How many total clock hours of tier education are required for journeyman licensure in Massachusetts?
Answer: 550 hours
The Board-approved tier program totals 550 clock hours — five tiers of 110 hours each (Tiers 1 through 5) — completed alongside the required apprentice work experience.

title: GENERAL: A licensed apprentice may complete Tier 1 and Tier 2 education (220 hours) in:
text:
A licensed apprentice may complete Tier 1 and Tier 2 education (220 hours) in:
Answer: A single calendar year
Per 248 CMR 11.02, a licensed apprentice may complete all 220 hours of Tier 1 and Tier 2 in a single calendar year. An unlicensed individual may complete Tier 1 prior to obtaining an apprentice license.

title: GENERAL: A graduate of an approved public vocational-technical high school plumbing program may receive credit of up to:
text:
A graduate of an approved public vocational-technical high school plumbing program may receive credit of up to:
Answer: 300 education hours and 1,700 experience hours
Per 248 CMR 11.02, eligible applicants may be granted up to 300 hours of education credit and 1,700 clock hours of experience credit from an approved Public Comprehensive High School Career/Vocational Technical School program.

title: GENERAL: Apprentice work experience toward journeyman licensure must be performed under the direct supervision of:
text:
Apprentice work experience toward journeyman licensure must be performed under the direct supervision of:
Answer: A Massachusetts licensed journeyman or master plumber
Per 248 CMR 11.02, the required clock hours must be worked as a licensed apprentice under the direct supervision of a Commonwealth of Massachusetts licensed journeyman or master plumber.

title: GENERAL: Which additional requirements apply to a candidate for the Master Plumber license?
text:
Which additional requirements apply to a candidate for the Master Plumber license?
Answer: One year as a licensed journeyman, 1,700 hours of work, and Tier 5 (110 hours)
A master candidate must have held a journeyman license for at least one year, documented 1,700 clock hours of qualifying work, and completed the 110-hour Tier 5 of the Board-approved five-tier education program.

title: GENERAL: How often must a Massachusetts plumbing license be renewed, and how much continuing education is required?
text:
How often must a Massachusetts plumbing license be renewed, and how much continuing education is required?
Answer: Every 2 years with 12 hours of CE
Per 248 CMR 11.04 (Mandatory Continuing Education), licenses renew on a two-year cycle and licensees must complete 12 hours of Board-approved continuing education as a condition of renewal.

title: GENERAL: Which 248 CMR section contains the education and experience standards for licensure?
text:
Which 248 CMR section contains the education and experience standards for licensure?
Answer: 248 CMR 11.00
248 CMR 11.00 is titled "Education and Experience Standards and Requirements for Licensure." 11.02 covers the apprentice/journeyman/master pathway; 11.04 covers mandatory continuing education.

title: GENERAL: An apprentice licensed BEFORE September 1, 2008 was required to complete how many clock hours of practical experience?
text:
An apprentice licensed BEFORE September 1, 2008 was required to complete how many clock hours of practical experience?
Answer: 8,000 clock hours
Apprentices licensed before September 1, 2008 fell under the older standard of 8,000 clock hours of practical work experience. The current pathway under 248 CMR 11.02 requires 6,800 clock hours paired with the tier education program.

title: PERMITS: Which section of 248 CMR governs the general conduct of plumbing and gas work, including business and apprentice licenses and inspector requirements?
text:
Which section of 248 CMR governs the general conduct of plumbing and gas work, including business and apprentice licenses and inspector requirements?
Answer: 248 CMR 3.00
Per 248 CMR 3.03, business and apprentice licenses, renewals, and inspector requirements sit in 248 CMR 3.00 — the general provisions governing the conduct of plumbing and gas work.

title: PERMITS: When water-testing a drainage system in sections under 248 CMR 10.04, no section may be tested with less than:
text:
When water-testing a drainage system in sections under 248 CMR 10.04, no section may be tested with less than:
Answer: A 10-foot head of water
Per 248 CMR 10.04, when the drainage system is tested in sections, each section must be subjected to at least a 10-foot head of water — the pressure the lowest joints will actually see in service.

title: PERMITS: Under 248 CMR 10.04, how long must water stay in the drainage system (or section under test) before the inspection starts?
text:
Under 248 CMR 10.04, how long must water stay in the drainage system (or section under test) before the inspection starts?
Answer: At least 15 minutes
248 CMR 10.04 requires the water to be kept in the system, or the portion under test, for at least 15 minutes before inspection begins — and the system must then be tight at all points.

title: PERMITS: An air test of the drainage system under 248 CMR 10.04 requires a uniform gauge pressure of:
text:
An air test of the drainage system under 248 CMR 10.04 requires a uniform gauge pressure of:
Answer: 5 PSIG (or 10 inches of mercury) held 15 minutes without added air
Per 248 CMR 10.04, the air test uses a uniform gauge pressure of 5 PSIG — or enough to balance a 10-inch column of mercury — held for at least 15 minutes with no additional air introduced. The gauge must read in increments no greater than 1/10 pound.

title: WATER: Per 248 CMR 10.04, a roughed water supply system must be tested and proved tight under a pressure of not less than:
text:
Per 248 CMR 10.04, a roughed water supply system must be tested and proved tight under a pressure of not less than:
Answer: 125 psi
248 CMR 10.04 requires the completed rough water supply system (or section) to be tested and proved tight at not less than 125 pounds per square inch.

title: DWV: Under 248 CMR 10.12, the air gap between an indirect waste and the building drainage system must be at least:
text:
Under 248 CMR 10.12, the air gap between an indirect waste and the building drainage system must be at least:
Answer: Twice the effective diameter of the drain served
Per 248 CMR 10.12, the air gap between the indirect waste and the building sanitary or storm drainage system must be at least twice the effective diameter of the drain served.

title: DWV: Which statement about trapping an indirect waste is correct under 248 CMR 10.12?
text:
Which statement about trapping an indirect waste is correct under 248 CMR 10.12?
Answer: The indirect waste must never be trapped ahead of the air gap or air-break
248 CMR 10.12 requires indirect wastes to discharge through an air gap or air-break, and in no instance may the indirect waste be trapped AHEAD of that air gap or air-break — a trap there would defeat the protection the gap provides. The receiving fixture (sink, floor drain) is itself trapped and vented.

title: DWV: An acceptable receptor for an indirect waste under 248 CMR 10.12 is:
text:
An acceptable receptor for an indirect waste under 248 CMR 10.12 is:
Answer: An open, accessible, properly trapped and vented sink or floor drain
Per 248 CMR 10.12, indirect waste piping may extend to an open, ACCESSIBLE individual waste sink, floor drain, or other fixture that is properly trapped and vented. Accessibility matters — a blocked receptor you can see gets fixed; a concealed one floods.

title: DWV: Under 248 CMR 10.13, a special waste system must adjust the pH of corrosive waste to what range before discharge?
text:
Under 248 CMR 10.13, a special waste system must adjust the pH of corrosive waste to what range before discharge?
Answer: Between 6 and 9
Per 248 CMR 10.13, special (corrosive/acid) wastes must be neutralized or treated so the pH lands between 6 and 9 before entering the drainage system — protecting both the piping and the treatment works downstream.

title: DWV: Per 248 CMR 10.13, the discharge from a special waste treatment system may connect to the building sanitary drain no closer than what distance from the neutralization system?
text:
Per 248 CMR 10.13, the discharge from a special waste treatment system may connect to the building sanitary drain no closer than what distance from the neutralization system?
Answer: 10 feet
248 CMR 10.13 allows the treated discharge to connect to the building sanitary drain or sewer, but in no case less than 10 feet from the neutralization system — keeping any still-aggressive waste away from the fresh connection.

title: DWV: How must an acid-neutralizing device be maintained with neutralizing medium under 248 CMR 10.13?
text:
How must an acid-neutralizing device be maintained with neutralizing medium under 248 CMR 10.13?
Answer: Automatically provided with sufficient neutralizing medium
Per 248 CMR 10.13, the neutralizing device must be AUTOMATICALLY provided with sufficient intake of neutralizing medium to render its contents non-injurious before discharge — the protection cannot depend on someone remembering to top it up.

title: DWV: Under 248 CMR 10.17, storm water:
text:
Under 248 CMR 10.17, storm water:
Answer: Shall not be drained into sewers intended for sewage only
Per 248 CMR 10.17, storm water shall not be drained into sewers intended for sanitary sewage only. Storm flows can overwhelm sanitary systems and treatment plants — the two systems stay separate.

title: MEDICAL: Under 248 CMR 10.18, how must sterilizers connect to the drainage system?
text:
Under 248 CMR 10.18, how must sterilizers connect to the drainage system?
Answer: Through individual and separate indirect wastes with proper air gaps
Per 248 CMR 10.18, every sterilizer gets an INDIVIDUAL and SEPARATE indirect waste with an air gap of not less than two diameters of the waste tailpiece — sterile equipment must be isolated from the drainage system by an open, visible gap.

title: MEDICAL: Per 248 CMR 10.18, where is the p-trap installed for a sterilizer's indirect waste?
text:
Per 248 CMR 10.18, where is the p-trap installed for a sterilizer's indirect waste?
Answer: On the discharge side of, and immediately below, the indirect waste connection
248 CMR 10.18 puts the p-trap on the discharge side of — and immediately below — the indirect waste connection serving each sterilizer. The trap protects the drainage side; the air gap above it protects the sterilizer.

title: MEDICAL: A bedpan steamer drain under 248 CMR 10.18 requires a trap with a minimum seal of:
text:
A bedpan steamer drain under 248 CMR 10.18 requires a trap with a minimum seal of:
Answer: 3 inches
Per 248 CMR 10.18, a bedpan steamer drain needs a trap with a minimum 3-inch seal, located between the fixture and the indirect waste connection — a deeper-than-normal seal for a fixture handling infectious waste under steam pressure.

title: MEDICAL: How many sterilizer wastes may drain to one trap in a battery assembly under 248 CMR 10.18?
text:
How many sterilizer wastes may drain to one trap in a battery assembly under 248 CMR 10.18?
Answer: Not more than three, with trap and waste sized to the combined fixture units
Per 248 CMR 10.18, a battery assembly of not more than THREE sterilizer wastes may drain to one trap, provided the trap and waste are sized for the combined fixture-unit rating.

title: MEDICAL: Under 248 CMR 10.18, a recess room containing the concealed portions of sterilizers must have:
text:
Under 248 CMR 10.18, a recess room containing the concealed portions of sterilizers must have:
Answer: At least one floor drain positioned to drain the entire floor area
Per 248 CMR 10.18, rooms containing recessed or concealed portions of sterilizers need at least one acceptable floor drain, connected to the drainage system and placed to drain the ENTIRE floor area — hidden equipment means leaks show up as floods.
